airplane: visible aircraft body with wings and tail, compact object-level structure, and clear airplane contours, distinguishing airplane from airport by lacking large terminal-scale paved surroundings and from runway by being a discrete aircraft object rather than an elongated strip.
airport: large aviation area with broad paved runways, terminal-like facilities, and organized airport infrastructure, distinguishing airport from runway by larger surrounding aviation context, from airplane by lacking a single compact fuselage object, and from industrial_area by emphasizing aviation pavement rather than factory compounds.
baseball_diamond: compact sports field with a clear diamond-shaped infield and surrounding outfield, distinguishing baseball_diamond from golf_course by lacking expansive landscaped fairways, from stadium by lacking a large enclosed spectator structure, and from ground_track_field by lacking an oval running-track pattern.
basketball_court: small rectangular court surface with clear hard-court markings, distinguishing basketball_court from tennis_court by court proportion and line layout and from mobile_home_park by lacking repeated trailer-like housing rows.
beach: bright shoreline region with clear sand-water boundary and open coastal texture, distinguishing beach from island by lacking a fully isolated landmass, from desert by direct water contact, and from sea_ice by warmer sand-like coastal appearance rather than frozen bright surface.
bridge: narrow man-made crossing structure spanning water or land, distinguishing bridge from harbor by lacking dense dock-side maritime infrastructure, from river by being a discrete crossing rather than a continuous channel, and from freeway by lacking a long extended road corridor.
chaparral: dry shrub-covered terrain with coarse natural texture and sparse woody vegetation, distinguishing chaparral from desert by slightly richer vegetation texture, from forest by lacking dense continuous canopy, and from mountain by weaker terrain relief and shadow structure.
church: prominent religious building or complex with distinctive landmark-like architecture and surrounding open space, distinguishing church from palace by less expansive ceremonial layout, from commercial_area by weaker dense urban business-block organization, and from medium_residential by lacking repeated neighborhood housing patterns.
circular_farmland: cultivated land with large regular circular irrigation patterns, distinguishing circular_farmland from rectangular_farmland by round parcel geometry, from terrace by lacking stepped contour bands, and from storage_tank by broader agricultural texture around circles rather than compact industrial tank clusters.
cloud: bright amorphous atmospheric mass with soft edges and no stable ground texture, distinguishing cloud from chaparral and mountain by lacking surface detail and from sea_ice by having softer irregular boundaries and less structured frozen-ground appearance.
commercial_area: dense urban business district with organized building blocks, roads, and large man-made structures, distinguishing commercial_area from industrial_area by lacking heavy factory compounds, from dense_residential by larger business-block structures, and from palace by weaker landmark-like symmetry and ceremonial grounds.
dense_residential: tightly packed residential roofs with very high housing density and minimal spacing, distinguishing dense_residential from medium_residential by much closer building intervals, from mobile_home_park by less uniform trailer-row organization, and from commercial_area by smaller repeated residential roofs rather than larger business blocks.
desert: broad barren region with dry homogeneous texture and very little vegetation, distinguishing desert from chaparral by weaker shrub texture, from mountain by less terrain relief, and from beach by lacking a clear shoreline water boundary.
forest: dense continuous tree canopy with dark green natural texture, distinguishing forest from chaparral by stronger canopy continuity, from meadow by denser vegetation cover, and from mountain by weaker relief and fewer exposed rocky slopes.
freeway: wide multi-lane transportation corridor with continuous linear flow and road-network structure, distinguishing freeway from overpass by emphasizing extended horizontal roadway, from intersection by lacking a compact junction node, and from runway by lacking aviation-strip markings and airport context.
golf_course: large landscaped green field with fairways, lawns, and designed open-course layout, distinguishing golf_course from baseball_diamond by lacking a compact diamond infield, from meadow by stronger man-made landscaping, and from tennis_court by lacking small repeated court rectangles.
ground_track_field: sports venue with an oval running track and central field, distinguishing ground_track_field from stadium by weaker enclosure, from baseball_diamond by lacking a diamond infield, and from tennis_court by lacking small rectangular court repetition.
harbor: waterfront maritime area with docks, vessels, and shore-adjacent port infrastructure, distinguishing harbor from ship by broader dock-and-shore context, from bridge by lacking a simple crossing structure, and from parking_lot by clear water-adjacent harbor organization.
industrial_area: large factory-like compounds with heavy infrastructure, storage yards, and production-oriented layouts, distinguishing industrial_area from thermal_power_station by lacking a power-plant-dominant structure, from railway_station by weaker rail-line concentration, and from storage_tank by not being dominated by circular tank clusters.
intersection: road junction where multiple transportation lines meet, distinguishing intersection from roundabout by lacking a central circular traffic island, from freeway by being a compact crossing node, and from mobile_home_park by lacking repeated housing units.
island: landmass completely surrounded by water with clear shoreline boundary, distinguishing island from beach by stronger enclosed land shape, from river by broader isolated land-water geometry, and from sea_ice by having land texture rather than frozen surface texture.
lake: large enclosed inland water body with smooth water surface and clear boundary, distinguishing lake from wetland by more uniform open water, from sea_ice by lacking frozen fractured texture, and from desert by dominant water appearance.
meadow: broad natural grass-covered open area with soft vegetation texture and weak structural boundaries, distinguishing meadow from forest by lacking dense canopy, from golf_course by weaker designed landscaping, and from rectangular_farmland by lacking regular cultivated parcel boundaries.
medium_residential: moderately spaced residential houses with visible yards and neighborhood streets, distinguishing medium_residential from mobile_home_park by less uniform trailer-row structure, from dense_residential by larger spacing, and from sparse_residential by denser neighborhood grouping.
mobile_home_park: repetitive small elongated housing units arranged in orderly rows, distinguishing mobile_home_park from medium_residential by stronger trailer-like regularity, from dense_residential by more uniform layout, and from tennis_court by lacking court markings and sports geometry.
mountain: rugged elevated terrain with strong relief, slope shadows, and irregular topographic texture, distinguishing mountain from desert by stronger terrain relief, from snowberg by less bright snow-dominant surface, and from chaparral by larger elevation structure.
overpass: elevated crossing transport structure with visible grade separation, distinguishing overpass from freeway by its crossing and bridge-like form, from bridge by stronger multi-road elevated traffic pattern, and from roundabout by lacking a circular traffic island.
palace: large landmark complex with symmetrical layout, open courtyards, and prominent architecture, distinguishing palace from church by more expansive ceremonial organization, from commercial_area by weaker dense urban block texture, and from tennis_court by lacking repeated small court rectangles.
parking_lot: large open paved area with organized parking rows and vehicle-oriented layout, distinguishing parking_lot from industrial_area by lacking dense factory compounds, from harbor by lacking strong dock-water context, and from freeway by lacking a continuous traffic corridor.
railway: elongated rail corridor with parallel tracks and linear transport structure, distinguishing railway from railway_station by lacking a concentrated station hub, from industrial_area by stronger track-line dominance, and from freeway by rail-line texture rather than paved highway lanes.
railway_station: transport hub with concentrated rail lines and station-related structures, distinguishing railway_station from railway by stronger station-node organization, from industrial_area by clearer rail concentration, and from airport by lacking long aviation runways.
rectangular_farmland: cultivated land divided into regular rectangular parcels, distinguishing rectangular_farmland from circular_farmland by angular field boundaries, from terrace by lacking stepped contour bands, and from meadow by stronger man-made agricultural organization.
river: elongated natural watercourse with continuous winding channel and visible banks, distinguishing river from bridge by being a water body rather than a crossing, from wetland by showing a more continuous channel, and from island by lacking a fully enclosed landmass.
roundabout: circular traffic junction with a central island and radiating roads, distinguishing roundabout from intersection by the visible circular center, from tennis_court by lacking court markings, and from dense_residential by road-dominant junction geometry.
runway: long straight paved strip with elongated linear geometry and open airport-like surroundings, distinguishing runway from airport by weaker terminal-scale context, from freeway by lacking complex road branching, and from airplane by lacking a discrete aircraft body.
sea_ice: bright frozen surface with irregular cracked or slab-like texture over water, distinguishing sea_ice from ship by lacking a discrete vessel shape, from lake by stronger frozen-surface texture, and from snowberg by flatter ice-field appearance rather than a compact snow-covered landform.
ship: discrete vessel object on water with elongated hull-like structure, distinguishing ship from harbor by lacking broad dock-side context, from sea_ice by clear object boundaries, and from bridge by being a floating object rather than a crossing structure.
snowberg: bright snow- or ice-covered elevated landform with strong cold-tone texture, distinguishing snowberg from mountain by stronger snow coverage, from sea_ice by more landform-like relief, and from chaparral by lacking vegetation texture.
sparse_residential: widely separated residential houses with large open gaps and low housing density, distinguishing sparse_residential from medium_residential by much larger spacing, from rectangular_farmland by repeated roof structures instead of crop parcels, and from church by lacking a single landmark-like central building.
stadium: large sports complex with prominent field and stronger enclosure or spectator-related structure, distinguishing stadium from baseball_diamond by larger scale, from ground_track_field by stronger venue framing, and from terrace by lacking stepped agricultural bands.
storage_tank: clusters of large circular industrial tanks with highly regular round geometry, distinguishing storage_tank from thermal_power_station by emphasizing tank clusters, from industrial_area by stronger circular-container dominance, and from circular_farmland by compact industrial circles without surrounding crop texture.
tennis_court: small rectangular court surfaces with clear line markings and repeated court geometry, distinguishing tennis_court from basketball_court by court layout, from medium_residential by lacking roof clusters, and from mobile_home_park by lacking trailer-like housing rows.
terrace: stepped agricultural or hillside bands following slope contours, distinguishing terrace from rectangular_farmland by contour-aligned layered structure, from circular_farmland by lacking circular irrigation patterns, and from stadium by lacking sports-field geometry.
thermal_power_station: large power-generation complex with heavy industrial structures, chimneys, or cooling-related facilities, distinguishing thermal_power_station from storage_tank by broader power-plant infrastructure, from industrial_area by more plant-specific heavy layout, and from commercial_area by lacking urban business-block organization.
wetland: water-rich natural area with mixed shallow water and vegetation patches, distinguishing wetland from lake by more fragmented water-vegetation texture, from river by less continuous channel structure, and from forest by visible water-dominant mixed surface.
